input.quote: This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0. This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (Section 4.0; mirrored in SOW Section 2.0) and Section 5.0 permits termination only "for cause" — material breach, insolvency events, change of control or force majeure (Section 5.1 a)–c)). There is no right for IBM to terminate for convenience at any point during the multi-year term; the only no-cause exit is a six-month (twelve-month under the SOW) non-renewal notice that bites only at the end of a term. That fails both the preferred position (30 days' notice) and the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a capped early-termination fee), and sits in walk-away territory ("no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term"). The PO-level cancellation right in SOW Section 6.1 lets us cancel individual Purchase Orders but does not give an agreement-level exit and is expressly subject to cost reimbursements, so it does not cure the gap. On the other side of the ledger the position is acceptable: MSL likewise has no mid-term convenience right and any non-renewal requires at least six months' notice, so no vendor-side redline is needed. We have therefore added a new Section 5.4 giving IBM a 30-day convenience right with a refund of prepayments, while preserving MSL's payment entitlements under Sections 5.2 and 5.3 and confirming MSL has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

proposal.summary: Add an IBM termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice, with refund of prepayments and no MSL mid-term convenience right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4.0 commits us to a three-year term and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause, so we have no exit for convenience; we have added a 30 days' notice convenience right with a refund of prepaid amounts, consistent with our playbook position. MSL's economics are protected because Sections 5.2 and 5.3 still govern payment for completed Products, work in process and Parts, and we are content that MSL has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

ops.text: Termination for Convenience. Notwithstanding Section 4.0, IBM may terminate this Agreement, any Statement of Work or Product Attachment, in whole or in part, for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL. IBM shall not be liable for any termination charge, penalty or other payment by reason of such termination, other than amounts payable to MSL for Products and Parts in accordance with Sections 5.2 and 5.3, and MSL shall refund to IBM any amounts prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination. MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement, any Statement of Work or any Product Attachment for convenience prior to the end of the then current term.
